Listen to this article Share ….Urges NUJ to push for members’ welfare The Labour Writers Association of Nigeria (LAWAN) has urged the federal government to develop affordable public transportation systems, including CNG-powered and electric vehicles, noting that temporary transport allowances were not substitutes for sustainable solutions. The association also called on the organised labour and the federal government to consult widely ahead of the next national minimum wage review in April 2027, insisting that wage adjustments must reflect inflation, the cost of living and workers’ declining purchasing power. The body made the call in a communique issued at the end of its 2026 annual workshop held in Lagos on October 30, with the theme: “Workers at the Centre of Nigeria’s Political Transition: Defending Rights, Advancing Welfare and Building Economic Justice.” The event attracted government officials and labour leaders from sectors of the economy, including Joe Ajaero, president of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC); Tubosun Olabiyi-Agoro, president of the Petroleum and Natural Gas Senior Staff Association of Nigeria (PENGASSAN), among others. LAWAN equally called on the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) to strengthen its trade union responsibilities by engaging media employers in collective bargaining negotiations to improve journalists’ salaries, working conditions and welfare benefits. It expressed concern over poor remuneration, job insecurity, inadequate pension arrangements and unfavourable working conditions confronting media workers across the country. It also urged media organisations to improve housing, healthcare, transportation and retirement benefits for journalists, while calling for the revival of the journalists’ housing scheme through partnerships with mortgage institutions. On the labour movement, LAWAN called on the NLC and Trade Union Congress (TUC) to resolve their differences and strengthen cooperation through a memorandum of understanding to advance workers’ interests. The association also advocated stronger social protection, improved pensioners’ welfare, responsible public sector reforms and greater transparency in the management of Nigeria’s natural resources. It urged journalists to deepen specialised labour reporting beyond strikes and industrial disputes to cover collective bargaining, employment policies, workers’ rights and social security. The conference maintained that sustainable economic growth requires decent wages, secure employment, effective social protection and a united labour movement.
